data.narrative:
Finwave Semiconductor is a Series A-stage chip company founded by Tomas Palacios and Bin Lu, operating within a competitive frontier-tech landscape anchored by 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private comparables including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor.

Valuation triangulation relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, given data constraints. The stage-progression approach applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the company's $25M total raised as a proxy baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $50M. Public-comparable anchoring is not applicable—while the 3 public semiconductor comps trade at a median 21.5x price-to-sales, Finwave's private revenue is not disclosed, precluding revenue multiple application. Peer-median analysis similarly cannot be applied; although 12 same-sector peers exist, the narrower filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) yield fewer than three datapoints required for statistical relevance.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, centered on $50M. This range reflects typical Series A progression dynamics but carries material uncertainty. Key risks to valuation include the absence of revenue disclosure (limiting public-comp anchoring), a fragmented private peer set with heterogeneous business models, and the early-stage nature of the company. The single-method reliance underscores that confidence in this range is moderate and contingent on operational traction and capital efficiency metrics not present in available data.
